sourcesOfTruth.title: NID Admissions 2027-28 Handbook: 5.5-year Integrated M.Des (NID Ahmedabad) and B.Des / Integrated M.Des (NID AP, MP, Haryana, Assam)
Designforge Self-Study Outline, Edition 02 (2026)
sourcesOfTruth.note: Designforge's method. Where it conflicts with a handbook, the handbook wins.

common.format: Paper-and-pencil or pen test, same time on the same day at every centre. Questions may involve text and visuals. English only.
common.duration: Stated on the admit card. Designforge practice papers run three hours.
common.prelimsWeightage: Used only to shortlist for the Mains. Not carried forward.
common.modeChangeCaveat: NID may change schedules or the nature and structure of exams, including moving them online, in unforeseen circumstances.
common.testCentreRule: A city can have more than one centre. NID may allot a centre that isn't your choice. The city can be changed only during the edit window.
common.noAccommodation: NID does not provide travel or accommodation for the Prelims or Mains.
common.cannotApplyBoth: Undergraduate programmes and the 2.5-year M.Des are examined simultaneously, so a candidate can apply for only one.
common.designforgeGuidance: The Designforge outline treats the Prelims as creative, observational and drawing-led, with no general-ability section, so this plan contains no GK, reasoning, English or quantitative drills.

programmes: 5.5-year Professional Education Master of Design (Integrated Pathway) at NID Ahmedabad, Bengaluru and Gandhinagar
4-year B.Des or 5.5-year Integrated M.Des at NID Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Haryana and Assam
ug.mainsShortlistRule: For each category, the number shortlisted equals 2.5 times the seats available.
ug.finalMerit: Calculated from DAT Mains marks using weightages NID will announce later.
ug.designforgeGuidance: Prepare for studio stamina, making under time and talking about your work. Do not display a fixed studio-to-in-person split: NID has not published one for 2027-28.

mains: Studio Test (group-wise; discipline-wise for Group X)
pg.mainsConductedBy: NID Ahmedabad for disciplines at Ahmedabad, Bengaluru and Gandhinagar. NID MP and NID Haryana run their own Mains.
pg.mainsShortlistRule: For each discipline, 4.5 times the seats available in each category applied for.
pg.finalMerit: Calculated from DAT Mains marks using weightages NID will announce later. Only candidates who attend both the Studio Test and Interview enter the final merit list.
pg.designforgeGuidance: Your portfolio and how you explain it carry the interview. Check the Mains notification for any portfolio requirements when NID publishes it.

ug.label: Last date to submit application and fee
Window to edit the application form
One-time window to edit the category certificate
Mains admit card, Studio Sensitivity Test, In-Person Sensitivity Test, results and counselling: to be announced

pg.label: Last date to submit application and fee
Window to edit the application form
One-time window to edit the category certificate
Mains admit card, Studio Test, Interview, results and counselling: to be announced

timeline.scorecardNote: Scorecards stay on the admissions website for only 20 days after each result. Download them immediately.

uploads.photo: Colour photograph taken at a professional studio, JPG/JPEG, 50 to 200 KB. Self-composed portraits are not accepted.
uploads.signature: Scanned or photographed signature, JPG/JPEG, 50 to 200 KB.
uploads.certificates: PDF, up to 1 MB. EWS and OBC-NCL certificates must be in the Central format, in the candidate's name, issued on or after 1 April 2026.

application.completeWhen: The application counts as complete only when you can view, download or print the auto-generated form after payment.

fees.note: Indian nationals, in rupees. For M.Des at NID Ahmedabad the fee is per discipline. Not refundable or transferable; bank charges extra.

eligibility.note: Show these as a reference and link to the handbook. Do not auto-decide eligibility.

ug.qualification: Passed or appearing for Class 12 (or equivalent) in any stream in 2026-27, passed in the first attempt; mark sheet by 15 July 2027.

pg.qualification: A bachelor's degree or equivalent in any discipline, or final-year candidates in 2026-27, with results by 31 July 2027. Design Education has its own qualification rules in the handbook.

otherNIDs.name: NID Assam
otherNIDs.note: B.Des with Industrial, Communication, and Textile & Apparel Design streams

GX.name: Group X
GX.note: Design Education has separate eligibility. Studio Test is discipline-wise for this group.

combinationRules.rule: Any one discipline from any group.
Two disciplines from the same group (not Group X), or one from Groups 1 to 5 plus one from Group X.
Two disciplines from the same group (not Group X), plus one from Group X.

pg.choicesLocked: Discipline choices cannot be changed later and applications are not transferable between disciplines.
pg.otherNIDsRule: A separate application is needed for each NID.

light.for: School or college students, or people with a job

intensive.for: Full-time aspirants with a free year

tiers.floor: Below eight hours a week the plan does not compress; it simply fails. If eight hours is genuinely the ceiling, the outline recommends a 24-week plan instead.

diagnostic.scale: 1 = never done this, 5 = do this reliably under time pressure

axes.name: Observation
axes.score5: You notice how things are made and where they fail, without being prompted, and you have written proof of it.
axes.fixDrill: Diary 'where it fails' quadrant and an extra field mission

axes.name: Drawing fluency
axes.score5: You can put a recognisable object in correct perspective, in context, in under five minutes.
axes.fixDrill: Your current drawing level's daily drill, timed

axes.name: Ideation speed
axes.score5: Ten distinct, non-trivial concepts in ten minutes, without stalling after the third.
axes.fixDrill: Ten-in-ten with the three-premise rule, then constraint flip

axes.name: Form and material
axes.score5: Given paper, wire and tape, you can build a standing, working object in twenty minutes.

axes.name: Articulation
axes.score5: You can explain any concept of yours in sixty seconds and answer ‘why not the opposite?’ well.
axes.fixDrill: Two recorded sixty-second pitches and explanation cards

axes.name: Awareness
axes.score5: You hold opinions about twenty designed things, Indian and global, and can defend them.
axes.fixDrill: Two index cards, then argue the opposite position for two minutes each

bands.name: Foundation first
bands.outlineAdvice: The outline recommends 24 weeks for this band.
bands.portalMessage: You have about 13 weeks. Run the plan as written, protect the four non-negotiables, and use the optional weak-axis block. Treat this attempt as calibration: the outline recommends starting the full plan again the day after the paper if this cycle is too soon.

bands.name: Standard build
bands.outlineAdvice: The 16-week spine, with one extra block a week for each of your two lowest axes.
bands.portalMessage: This is a compressed plan for you. Protect the non-negotiables and add the weak-axis block for your lowest axis each week.

bands.name: Sharpening
bands.outlineAdvice: The 12-week compression. Skip foundational drawing drills; spend the time on simulation volume, portfolio depth and articulation.
bands.portalMessage: This plan is your compression. Full simulations start in week 4, and Drawing L0 is skipped.

diagnostic.rescoreRule: Re-score without looking at the first answers. A score that has not moved on an axis in six weeks means the drill isn't working: change the drill, not the effort.
diagnostic.skipL0Rule: Skip Drawing L0 if the drawing axis scored 3 or more.

nonNegotiables: The 45-minute daily drill, six days a week
One Sunday review, written, thirty minutes
One full simulation a week from week 7 (outline: week 9 in the 16-week spine)

weeklyOperatingSystem.what: 15 min observation sketch from life, 20 min the skill of the current week, 10 min logging what broke. Same time every day.
Deep work on the week's theme. Phone in another room.
Someone other than you says what is wrong with the week's output.
Written: what improved, what did not, what changes next week.

practiceRules: Time-box everything, including the small things.
Cut feedback latency: review within 48 hours.

frame: What do you think this is doing?
withoutMentor: Cold-read yesterday's work first thing in the morning.
Trade work weekly with two other aspirants on a fixed day.
Explain it aloud, recorded, and note every hesitation.

weeklyThemes: Things held in one hand while doing something else
Repairs: how Indians fix what breaks
Anything a child under six operates
Interfaces used by people who did not choose them
diary.fieldMissionBrief: 90 minutes, notebook, no phone. Come back with twelve sketches and three failures observed.

checkpoints.target: 24 diary pages; name three failures in objects you use daily
60+ diary pages; patterns appearing across entries

drawingLevels.drill: Straight lines, ellipses, parallel hatching: 10 min, no ruler, wrist locked
drawingLevels.pass: Ellipses close cleanly and lines are confident single strokes

drawingLevels.drill: Cubes, cylinders, cones in one- and two-point perspective from imagination
drawingLevels.pass: You can rotate a cube to an arbitrary angle without measuring

drawingLevels.drill: Real objects built from primitives: mixer, torch, stapler, chair
drawingLevels.pass: A stranger identifies the object immediately, from any of three angles

drawingLevels.drill: Shading, cast shadow, and rendering glass, steel, cloth, cane, terracotta
drawingLevels.pass: Material reads correctly in greyscale without labels

drawingLevels.drill: Figures in proportion, in action, in a place, from memory
drawingLevels.pass: Figures carry weight and scenes have a believable ground plane

drawingLevels.drill: Object, user and context in five minutes, then four, then three
drawingLevels.pass: A legible, annotated concept sketch in under four minutes

examinersLookFor: Context: the hand, the surface, the moment of use
Annotation: two words with a leader line
kit: A cheap A4 sketchbook, 2B pencil, 0.5 black fineliner, one grey marker, one red pen for annotation.

methods: Eight concepts, eight minutes, one per fold. No editing.
Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify, Put to other use, Eliminate, Reverse, in sequence on one object.
List the brief's assumptions, negate one, design for the negation.
Pair the brief with a random unrelated object or system and find the bridge.
Design the worst solution, then invert each property.
Find another domain that solved the same structural problem and import its mechanism.
Six people, three ideas, five minutes, then pass and build on your neighbour's.
convergenceCriteria: Does it answer the brief as written?
Is it feasible with plausible material?
Is it different from the other nine?
Can I draw it clearly in four minutes?
Can I explain why it exists in one line?

tenInTen.rule: One brief, ten distinct concepts, ten minutes, a thumbnail each. Count how many arrive after minute six.
tenInTen.target: Six or more post-minute-six concepts by week 12

ideation.threePremiseRule: At least three concepts in a set must attack the problem from a different user, mechanism or definition of the problem.

buildingDrills.name: Stand it up
buildingDrills.brief: A 30 cm structure from one A4 sheet that supports a book.

buildingDrills.name: Join without glue
buildingDrills.brief: Connect two card pieces five ways: slot, tab, fold, weave, tension.

buildingDrills.name: Make it move
buildingDrills.brief: One hinge, one slider, one rotating joint, from card alone.

buildingDrills.name: Hold water
buildingDrills.brief: A vessel from flat material that doesn't leak for sixty seconds.

buildingDrills.name: Grip it
buildingDrills.brief: A handle for a specific hand doing a specific task: wet, gloved, arthritic, a child's.

buildingDrills.name: Compress it
buildingDrills.brief: An object that folds to a quarter of its volume and returns.

buildingDrills.name: One material, three forms
buildingDrills.brief: The same sheet of card, three completely different objects.

buildingDrills.name: Blind build
buildingDrills.brief: Build to a written brief without drawing first. Then draw what you built.

buildRules.materials: Paper, card, wire, thread, tape, scissors, a blade. Nothing else.
buildRules.photograph: Every model, three angles, plain background, decent light, the moment it's finished.
materialQuestions: Which Indian craft uses it well?

explanationCard: What breaks: the exact failure moment today
The move: your intervention, in one sentence
Why this and not the obvious one
What it costs: the trade-off you accepted

pitchStructure: The problem as you framed it
writingDrills: 250 words a week on a designed thing you encountered: describe, judge, justify.
Rewrite five briefs as single sentences beginning ‘How might we…’.
Restate one brief three ways and note how each opens different solutions.
questionBank: Why design? Why not the thing your marks qualify you for?
Which of these is your weakest piece, and why?
What would you change if you started again?
Whose work do you admire, and what specifically about it?
Show me something badly designed that you use every day.
What did you make most recently, outside of exam preparation?
What have you read or watched in the last month?
What would you do if you did not get in this year?
articulation.bankOfTwenty: Twenty things you can speak about for two minutes each, from your diary and builds.
articulation.tenPositions: Ten opinions about design you can hold under disagreement.

indexCardFields: One example you have seen yourself
One sentence of your own opinion
awareness.test: Someone picks a card and argues the opposite. If you can't hold your ground for two minutes, you have facts but no view.
awareness.twentyThingsRule: Mix the celebrated with the everyday. At least half Indian, and at least five things you dislike.

indianLineage: The India Report and the founding of NID
The Eameses' visit and what it argued for
Khadi and design as a political instrument
Folk and tribal traditions and their contemporary misuse
Craft clusters and the artisan economy
contemporaryIndia: Railway signage, metro wayfinding, currency, the rupee symbol
Digital public goods and their interface problems
global: The UN Sustainable Development Goals as design briefs

errorBuckets.name: Concept
errorBuckets.example: All ten concepts were the same idea

errorBuckets.name: Time
errorBuckets.example: Ran out of time in the last question
errorBuckets.fix: Time-boxed thumbnails; hard stop at 60% of allotted time

errorBuckets.name: Clarity
errorBuckets.example: The examiner could not tell what the object was
errorBuckets.fix: Every sketch gets a user, a surface, two labels

errorLedgerRule: An error logged three times is a gap in method: it needs a drill, not more effort.
reviewProtocol: Score it before you feel anything.
Put every error in exactly one bucket.
Count the buckets; the dominant one is this week's repair target.
Log it in the ledger and close the paper.

weekCompletionCheck: One redo from two weeks ago

spine: Where this sits, and for whom. One paragraph.
The problem as you framed it, not as it was handed to you.
What you observed or tested: photographs, notes, quotes.
The concepts you rejected, and honestly why.
What changed between versions, and what forced the change.
What failed, and what you would do differently now.
shape: Lead with your strongest, close with your second strongest
failures: Process invented afterwards to justify a finished image
Group work with no statement of what you did
Software showreels with no problem attached
Every project a success, no evidence of judgement
Text too dense to read, or too thin to assess

structure: Open with a specific thing you did or noticed
Trace the line from it to this application
Name what you want to work on, and why here
Admit a gap and how you'll close it
sop.edit: Cut it by a third: remove every sentence that could appear in someone else's statement.

ug.studio: Long studio briefs, materials restricted, no phone, no reference. Rotate making-led, drawing-led, narrative and group formats. Budget the last 20% of time for presentation.
ug.inPerson: Weekly rehearsal from week 8 with someone who pushes back. Carry twenty things you can talk about and ten opinions you can defend. Think aloud. Bring the sketchbook.

pg.studio: Timed domain studio sets in your group's format.
pg.interview: Mock interviews weekly from week 8; every project rehearsed to sixty seconds; portfolio and statement of purpose finished.

mainsPrep.materialsTest: Two weeks before, do one full brief using only what you intend to carry, and note what fails. Check official instructions for what is permitted and provided.

readFoundations: The Design of Everyday Things (Donald Norman)
The India Report (Charles and Ray Eames)
readDrawingMaking: Sketching: Drawing Techniques for Product Designers (Koos Eissen and Roselien Steur)
Drawing on the Right Side of the Brain (Betty Edwards)
Universal Principles of Design (Lidwell, Holden and Butler)
follow: Student portfolios from your target programme
go: Your nearest craft cluster or artisan workshop
A working railway station on a weekday
A degree show at a design institute
resources.pastPapers: Use official past papers first. Solve every question before reading any solution, then write your own justification.
resources.rule: Pick two books, two films and two ongoing sources for the whole plan.

conflictsResolved.handbook: UG: 2.5× seats per category (handbook-ug §2.1, §8.4, §9.3). PG: 4.5× seats per discipline per category (handbook-pg §9.3)

conflictsResolved.decision: Do not show a split. Describe both parts as substantial.
Practice papers run three hours; label it as Designforge practice, not an exam fact.

conflictsResolved.handbook: NID Ahmedabad now offers a 5.5-year Integrated M.Des; B.Des is at NID AP, MP, Haryana, Assam (handbook-ug §4)
conflictsResolved.decision: Call the track ‘B.Des and Integrated M.Des (after Class 12)’.

conflictsResolved.outline: ‘A limited number of disciplines within one faculty stream’ (outline §12)
conflictsResolved.handbook: One to three disciplines, with group rules and Group X (handbook-pg §4.1)
conflictsResolved.decision: Use the handbook rules and validate them in onboarding.

conflictsResolved.handbook: Studio Test and Interview; portfolio not mentioned (handbook-pg §8.4)
conflictsResolved.decision: Keep portfolio prep as Designforge guidance and tell students to check the Mains notification.
Week 8 only; week 14 falls after the exam in a 13-week plan.
